topic.title: Diwali has one film
topic.claim: At Diwali the family picks one film and every other release loses, because a festival ticket is a group decision and not a taste decision.
topic.behaviour: Families book seats together and choose what everyone, including the grandmother, can sit through. The weekend chart was lopsided: Ramayana took ₹174.00 crore of the top five's ₹252.75 crore net, and Jailer 2 and AK 47 slipped mainly because they lost screens.
topic.mechanism: Theatres give shows to whatever fills the hall, and groups fill the hall for the film that is safe for all ages. A hit gets more screens, which makes it look even bigger.
topic.group: People who go to the movies with family at festival time
topic.moment: You wanted to see a different film this Diwali, but the family plan had one name on it.

turn.believed: The biggest film wins because it is the best film.
turn.actually: It wins because a group of different ages can agree on it, and screens then follow the crowd.

topic.feeling: Part of a crowd and slightly left out of your own choice
topic.villain: A screen-allocation system that rewards whatever fills the hall in the first weekend
topic.because: Exhibitors earn from full halls, so they move shows to the film families choose. The second-choice film loses its place even if people liked it.

proof.fact: Sacnilk puts the top five films at ₹252.75 crore net for the Diwali weekend, with Ramayana taking ₹174.00 Cr (69% of that). Jailer 2 and AK 47 slipped mainly because they lost screens.

topic.payoff: A festival hit is the film the whole family could say yes to, not necessarily the one anyone loved most.
topic.send_to: The friend who always ends up watching what the family picks
real_details: Scene grew on both Saturday and Sunday, unlike the usual front-loaded star release
topic.news_peg: Sacnilk's Diwali weekend (November 6-8) box office report (2026-11-09)
topic.why_now: The Diwali weekend numbers have just come out.

score.why: A festival ticket is a group decision, not a taste decision. The box-office fact supports the argument instead of being the point.
